sentenceSets.sentence: She had become a redoubtable figure in the field, someone whose opposition to a proposal was taken seriously even when the proposal had merit.

answerChoices.reasoning: This word points to presence and bearing, but the sentence measures her standing entirely by the weight her objections carry among colleagues.
The sentence never says anyone is frightened of her; it says her opposition can sink even a meritorious proposal, which is about influence rather than fear.
This suggests someone unapproachable or grim in manner, yet the sentence describes how her judgments are received, not how she comes across socially.
Commanding implies she directs others, but the sentence shows her power operating from outside, as an objector whose resistance others cannot dismiss.
Too mild for a figure whose disapproval can outweigh a proposal's actual merit, which is what the concessive clause emphasizes.
Respect would not explain why sound proposals lose ground merely because she objects to them.
This describes reliability of expertise, whereas the sentence is about the effect of her opposition regardless of whether the proposal is good.
Visibility alone would not cause colleagues to treat her objections as decisive.
Someone whose opposition is taken seriously is by definition not being ignored.
The sentence shows her openly opposing proposals, which is not the behavior of a hesitant person.
An unknown person could not be described as a figure in the field whose views others weigh.

sentenceSets.sentence: The visiting side arrived with a redoubtable back line that had conceded only three goals in an entire season.

answerChoices.reasoning: This word emphasizes the terror a unit inspires, while the sentence rests its case on a defensive record that opponents have failed to break down.
Three conceded goals show the defense has in fact been beaten, if rarely, so a word meaning never subdued overstates what the statistic reports.
Stalwart stresses loyal, dependable service over time, but the sentence highlights how formidable the unit is to face rather than how faithful it is.
The record given includes goals conceded, so the defense does yield occasionally; the sentence claims excellence, not absolute impermeability.
Discipline describes how the players behave, whereas the sentence is concerned with the threat the back line poses to the team facing it.
Nothing in the sentence mentions the defenders' age or years of experience, only their record over one season.
The sentence cites the statistic itself rather than any public acclaim attached to the unit.
Far too tepid for a defense whose record is offered as the reason the visiting side is worth worrying about.
A leaky defense contradicts the figure of three goals conceded all season.
The statistic presents the back line as remarkably successful, not luckless.
A full season of near-flawless defending is offered as evidence against, not for, rawness.

sentenceSets.sentence: The mountain's north face remains a redoubtable ascent, attempted by fewer than a dozen climbers each season.

answerChoices.reasoning: Daunting names the discouragement climbers feel, but the sentence points to the route's own severity, evidenced by how few will take it on.
This emphasizes physical toll during the climb, while the sentence gives only the number of people willing to start it.
Treacherous implies hidden dangers that deceive, and the sentence supplies no detail about loose rock, crevasses, or unstable conditions.
Arduous stresses sustained labor, yet a merely laborious route would not scare off all but a dozen climbers a year.
The sentence reports low participation rather than deaths, accidents, or risk statistics.
Ordinary strain does not explain why the face is singled out as still unconquered by most; plenty of well-traveled routes are strenuous.
Nothing in the sentence describes the specific skills, gear, or moves the route demands.
This describes the route's reputation among the public, but the sentence characterizes the climb itself and then cites attempt numbers as proof.
An easy route would not deter all but a handful of climbers each season.
The low number of attempts marks the ascent as anything but a casual undertaking.
The sentence says nothing about views; it explains why almost nobody tries the route.
